properties.description: The served `why` skill (`/why`): an interview in two walks — by feature (why does this exist?) and by change (why did it change?) — over a repository's history, recording reasons, needs, choices and never-undo rules on the owner's word and nothing about structure. `tools/why_history.py`, shipped in the kit, reads the git main line as the agenda: changes grouped as a person would recognise them, noise dropped by rule and counted, reverts flagged, one feature's changes as a numbered page, and coverage computed from the design export (ChangeEvent `commits`, open follow-ups, a `why_cursor` finding per feature) rather than kept in a second record. Adopt's intent-recovery phase points to it.
properties.name: Why an existing system is the way it is is recorded by interviewing its designer
